'''''Clerodendrum speciosissimum''''' is a [[tropical shrub]] of the family [[Lamiaceae]], native to [[Indonesia]] and [[Papuasia]], but now naturalized in parts of [[Latin America]], [[Africa]], the [[Caribbean]], [[Seychelles]], and [[Florida]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=43058 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>Friedmann, F. (1994). Flore des Seychelles Dicotylédones: 1-663. ORSTOM éditions.</ref><ref>Mabberley, D.J. & De Kok, R.P.J. (2004). Labiatae. Flore de la Nouvelle-Calédonie et Dépendances 25: 20-141. Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle, Paris.</ref><ref>Sita, P. & Moutsambote, J.-M. (2005). Catalogue des plantes vasculaires du Congo, ed. sept. 2005: 1-158. Bothalia 41: 41-82.</ref><ref>Davidse, G. & al. (eds.) (2012). Flora Mesoamericana 4(2): 1-533. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, México, D.F.</ref><ref>Acevedo-Rodríguez, P. & Strong, M.T. ==Description==
The shrub can grow up to 4 m tall. The leaves are square-shaped, and the large [[heart-shaped]] flowers can reach up to 30 cm. It is cultivated as an ornamental plant, in particular for its bright red flowers.
